problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+1)^{2}(y+2).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\le 0?$
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/26f786cb4b0e0d923502a6fef4c827341a5a8c5f61d497ec479742db3ee7ea87.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/0f68fc744e359192c65134f941952d8cfcf928b1f74924896df09ea23a36d07f.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+1)^{2}$ | $(y+2)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-2,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(0,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,-3)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(0,-3)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\le 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/206cc195b55db8f3793f4d84d0bd3b78f21430759770c8be4c815f8db8d562fb.png)
